question: We are choosing business internet for a 28-person office. Priorities: daytime video-call stability and reachable human support; ignore speed theater. Write a short research-style recommendation memo from the retrieved sources only. Candidates: Meridian Broadband, Blue Harbor Connect, Yangtze Node, Silk Route Networks, Anchorpoint Telecom, Verdant Wire, Cathay Link, Northwind Telecom, Lantern Fibre, Pearl Grid Networks. End with a numbered list of all ten from best to worst.

web_snippets.excerpt: Northwind Telecom had the fewest daytime packet-loss tickets in a 40-office panel.
Verdant Wire support answered chat in under ten minutes three times last month.
Cathay Link same-day ticket replies and a reachable account team helped one Shanghai office recover quickly; daytime video is usually fine, with rare stutter on older last-mile segments.
Anchorpoint Telecom coverage map is wide; last-mile quality varies block to block.
Stability-first buyers still lean Northwind; support-speed buyers lean Verdant; Cathay Link is the compromise pick when account responsiveness matters as much as raw uptime.

notes: Contested evidence: two competitors look stronger on stated priorities; principal only in mixed tradeoff notes. No answer-key ranking.
